title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Standards & Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This page consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response standards, canonical runbook structure, postmortem template, rotation and escalation policies, recommended game-day exercises, and reusable status page / customer communication templates. Use this page as the source of truth for operational behavior during incidents and for onboarding new on-call engineers.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-restore (MTTR) for Sev1/Sev0 incidents.
- Ensure clear roles and responsibilities during incidents.
- Provide reproducible runbooks and communication templates to reduce cognitive load.
- Capture actionable postmortems and follow-up ownership.

Scope and ownership
- Applies to: Redwood-hosted control-plane services, serving runtime components, and customer-facing status pages.
- Owner team: engineering (eng-sre maintains standards; teams owning individual services are responsible for runbook accuracy and runbook tests).
- Exceptions: customer-sensitive incidents requiring legal/security coordination should follow security-and-compliance escalation (see related_pages).

Incident severity definitions
1) Severity levels (standard):
   - SEV0 (Critical / Production Down): Total outage for a majority of customers or data loss. Immediate PagerDuty page, Executive notification within 15 minutes.
   - SEV1 (High / Degraded): Significant functional impact (e.g., inference latency > 5x SLO for > 15 minutes, large fraction of requests failing). PagerDuty page; primary on-call leads incident.
   - SEV2 (Medium): Partial degradation or isolated customer impact; ticket + Slack alert for the owning team.
   - SEV3 (Low): Informational or minor bug; tracked in the backlog.

SLO & alert thresholds (examples)
- Serving runtime request success rate SLO: 99.5% per 1m window.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 250ms. Alert: P95 > 500ms for 5m -> SEV1.
- Error rate: 5xx rate > 1% for 10m -> SEV1.
- Queue/backlog depth: GPU queue length > 3x target for 5m -> SEV1.
(Teams should publish service-specific SLOs in the SLO playbook and link them from the service runbook.)

Pager and escalation policy
- Primary on-call receives the initial page. If unacknowledged in 5 minutes -> secondary on-call. If still unacknowledged in 10 minutes total -> oncall-manager and SRE lead escalate.
- For SEV0: auto-call + SMS escalation. Notify product and customer success for impacted customers.

Roles and responsibilities during an incident
- Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination, triage decisions, customer comms cadence, and post-incident review.
- Primary on-call (Service Owner): executes runbook steps, triages the root cause, applies mitigations.
- Secondary on-call: supports primary and handles escalations.
- Communications lead: posts updates to status page and customer comms (can be IC or a delegated person).
- Scribe: captures timeline, commands executed, links to dashboards.
- Engineering lead: approves any intrusive mitigations or rollback.

Incident lifecycle (high-level)
1) Detection & Triage
   - Alert fires -> page is delivered.
   - Primary on-call acknowledges and assigns IC.
   - Validate impact and classify severity.
2) Contain & Mitigate
   - Follow the service runbook to apply short-term mitigations (traffic split, disable feature flags, scale up capacity).
   - If mitigation requires cross-team work, create a dedicated Slack channel and invite stakeholders.
3) Restore & Validate
   - Restore service for customers and validate against SLOs and synthetic tests.
4) Communicate
   - Use status page + templated customer comms (see templates below).
5) Post-incident
   - Run retrospective within 3 business days; publish a postmortem within 7 business days with action items and owners.

Runbook standards and template
Every service must maintain an up-to-date runbook at the service wiki entry. Runbooks should be executable by an on-call engineer who is familiar with the service but not the original implementer. Minimum sections:
- Title & service overview (1-2 paragraphs).
- Owner & escalation contacts (PagerDuty ID, Slack handles, primary, secondary).
- Relevant SLOs & alert rules (links to metrics dashboards).
- Quick triage checklist (what to check in the first 5 minutes).
- Mitigations (ordered, low-risk first).
- Recovery verification steps.
- Postmortem checklist & link to template.
- Test instructions (how to run a runbook drill).

Runbook quick-check checklist (first 5 minutes)
- Check the service health dashboard (link).
- Confirm alert details and time window.
- Verify deployment / recent changes (CI/CD deploys, config changes).
- Check downstream/upstream dependencies (e.g., model registry, storage, k8s node health).
- Look for rate-limiting or quota errors in logs.

Sample runbook mitigation steps (example for serving runtime high-latency alert)
1) Validate: run curl against a warm instance and measure latency.
2) Identify hotspot: check GPU utilization (nvidia-smi), request queue depth, and recent model swaps.
3) Short-term mitigation: move traffic to a lower-latency region or fallback model variant (use routing policy in the console).
4) If queue backlog, temporarily increase batcher workers or scale up pool (document CLI commands here).
5) If degraded kernel path suspected, rollback last model runtime change.
6) Verify by running the synthetic load tests and confirm P95 < 250ms.

Commands & examples (replace placeholders)
- Check pods: kubectl --context prod get pods -n runtime | grep servicing
- Review logs (last 30m): kubectl --context prod logs -n runtime -l app=serving --since=30m | head
- Scale pool: rcli pool scale --pool-id {pool} --replicas {N}  # internal CLI

Postmortem template (required fields)
- Title
- Severity
- Incident window (start/end UTC)
- Summary (3-sentence operational summary)
- Timeline (ordered, timestamped events)
- Root cause analysis (technical and human factors)
- Detection & response effectiveness (what worked, what didn't)
- Action items (owner, due date, acceptance criteria)
- Follow-ups (link to related PRs, runbook updates, monitoring changes)
- Postmortem author & reviewers

Runbook testing and game days
- Each service must run at least one runbook drill per quarter. Drills should be listed in the service's runbook and scheduled with eng-sre.
- Game day types:
  - Warm-up (low-risk checks, notification verification).
  - Fault-injection (simulate degraded latency, memory pressure).
  - Full outage (simulate regional failure, practice failover).
- Game day template: scope, objectives, scenario steps, success criteria, participant list, and post-game playbook.
- Track outcomes in a shared spreadsheet and ensure action items have owners and dates.

On-call rotations and handoffs
- Typical cadence: primary rotation is 1 week. Secondary rotation mirrors primary.
- Handoffs: mandatory Monday morning handoff post (Slack) with current open incidents, ongoing mitigations, and any planned changes for the week.
- Handoff checklist:
  - Confirm PagerDuty schedule is up to date.
  - Share known issues, rollouts, and customer-impacting changes.
  - Verify access (k8s, internal tooling, credentials).

Mental health & burnout mitigation
- Enforce 48 hours buffer after a SEV0 before assigning the person to another SEV0 incident.
- Encourage rotation swaps for personal time; managers must approve extended absences.
- Use incident intensity score (0-10) to flag follow-up counseling or reduced on-call load.

Status page & customer communication templates
- Status page principles: timely, transparent, non-speculative, and actionable. Provide timeline and what customers should expect.

Status page templates (short updates):
- Investigating: "We are investigating reports of increased request latency for the Redwood inference API in region us-west-2. Our engineers are actively triaging; next update in 15 minutes."
- Identified: "We have identified a service-level regression tied to a recent runtime kernel change that increases P95 latency. We are rolling back the change and expect restoration within 30 minutes."
- Mitigated/Monitoring: "We have mitigated the impact by failing over traffic to a stable model variant. Customers may see intermittent errors while we validate; P95 latency is trending down. Next update in 60 minutes."
- Resolved: "The issue has been resolved. Root cause: a runtime kernel regression triggered by a kernel selector mismatch during recent rollout. A complete postmortem will be published within 7 business days."

Customer email template (use for targeted customers):
Subject: Redwood status — Impact to inference latency (region us-west-2)
Body:
Hi <CustomerName>,

We wanted to inform you of an incident affecting inference latency in us-west-2 between <start> and <end> UTC. We applied a mitigation (traffic failover to a verified model variant) and restored service within <time-to-restore>. There may be a short period of degraded performance while we validate.

What happened: brief technical summary in plain language.
What we did: steps taken to mitigate and restore.
What we're doing next: follow-up actions and timeline; link to postmortem when available.

If you have any questions or saw customer-impacting behavior, please reply or contact your account team.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support & Engineering

Communication cadence guidance
- SEV0: update every 15 minutes until mitigated, then every 60 minutes until resolved.
- SEV1: update every 30 minutes until mitigated, then every 4 hours until resolved.
- Include clear next update ETA and contact info for urgent escalation.

Post-incident review and action tracking
- Postmortem owner must publish within 7 business days. Postmortems require at least one engineering reviewer and one product or support reviewer for customer-impacting incidents.
- Action items should be small, measurable, and assigned with due dates. Track actions in the team backlog and reference them in the postmortem.

Templates & attachments (where to find)
- Canonical runbook template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-template
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template
- Status page examples & CDN config: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-templates
- Game day scheduling form: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-day-request-form

FAQ
Q: Who declares the incident SEV level?
A: The IC in consultation with the primary on-call and eng-sre on-call lead. If uncertain, classify higher and de-escalate.
Q: How do we handle incidents affecting a single enterprise customer requiring PII/contract sensitivity?
A: Mark confidentiality as restricted and follow security-and-compliance escalation. Notify legal and customer success immediately.

Change history
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft and adoption by eng-sre.
- 2026-02-15: Updated escalations, added game-day cadence, and clarified communication templates.

Appendix: quick links and contact list
- PagerDuty schedule: https://pagerduty.redwood.example/schedules
- Incident Slack channel template: #incidents-{incident-id}
- Status page: https://status.redwood.example
- On-call manager: @carlos.gomez

If you find gaps in these standards or want to propose changes, open a PR against the page and add reviewers from eng-sre and the owning service.
